ai_summary: Great Britain’s wind generation currently stands at 5.2 GW, with estimated Scottish wind output contributing 2.2 GW, which represents 21.8% of installed Scottish wind capacity. A stark regional divergence is visible in grid decarbonisation: Scottish carbon intensity sits at 0 gCO2/kWh versus 206 gCO2/kWh GB-wide. However, persistent cross-border transmission bottlenecks prevent this abundant green electricity from reaching southern demand centres. Consequently, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has already reached 41.1 GWh through Balancing Mechanism turn-down bids, incurring an immediate constraint cost of about £1,427,690. To compensate for this stranded green energy, an estimated 7,806,834 m3 of gas was burned elsewhere on the system, injecting 14,381 tonnes of CO2 into the atmosphere. Annualising today's expenditure reveals an estimated total yearly cost of £521 million for curtailment. This grid friction places an unnecessary financial load on end-users, delivering an estimated increase of roughly £1.80/MWh on everybody's invoice in the UK. Without expedited transmission investments, consumers will continue paying twice: first to curtail clean Scottish generation, and again to burn fossil fuels in its place.
